extracted.intended_audience: ICML 2020 reviewers / program committee members (conference peer reviewers in machine learning)
extracted.subtask_description: The official reviewer form used by ICML 2020 for evaluating submitted machine-learning conference papers, covering summary, merits, overall score, detailed comments, reviewer expertise/confidence, dataset norms, and meta-reviewer-only items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Please summarize the main claim(s) of this paper in two or three sentences.
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for a concise 2-3 sentence summary of the paper's main claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers. (Forms notes visibility semantics: when visible to other reviewers, that happens only after they have submitted their own reviews.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits of the Paper
rubrics_metrics.description: What would be the main benefits to the machine learning community if this paper were presented at the conference? Please list at least one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Please provide an overall evaluation for this submission.
rubrics_metrics.description: An overall categorical evaluation with the following choices: Outstanding paper, I would fight for it to be accepted.; Very good paper, I would like to see it accepted.; Borderline paper, but has merits that outweigh flaws.; Borderline paper, but the flaws may outweigh the merits.; Below the acceptance threshold, I would rather not see it at the conference.; Wrong or known results, I would fight to have it rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond what you've written above as 'merits', state the major considerations that led you to your overall score for this paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required field. Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed Comments for Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Freeform detailed comments covering, as relevant: the significance and novelty of the paper's contributions; the paper's potential impact on the field of machine learning; the degree to which the paper substantiates its main claims; constructive criticism and feedback to improve the work or presentation; the degree to which the results are reproducible; missing references, presentation suggestions, and typos or grammar improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required. Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Please rate your expertise on the topic of this submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessed reviewer expertise with choices: I have published one or more papers in the narrow area of this submission.; I have closely read papers on this topic, and written papers in the broad area of this submission.; I have seen talks or skimmed a few papers on this topic, and have not published in this area.; I have little background in the area of this submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required. Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers. Use to communicate domain knowledge level that informs interpretation of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Please rate your confidence in your evaluation of this paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessed confidence in the review with choices: I am very confident in my evaluation of the paper. I read the paper very carefully and I am very familiar with related work.; I tried to check the important points carefully. It is unlikely, though possible, that I missed something that could affect my ratings.; I am willing to defend my evaluation, but it is fairly likely that I missed some details, didn't understand some central points, or can't be sure about the novelty of the work.; Not my area, or the paper was hard for me to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required. Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers. Guides weight given to the reviewer's judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets (norms checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: If this paper introduces a new dataset, which of the following norms are addressed? Options: This paper does not introduce a new dataset (skip the remainder of this question).; A link to the dataset is provided in the paper.; The dataset is deposited in a repository that ensures long term preservation of the data.; The dataset has a persistent identifier such as Digital Object Identifier or Compact Identifier.; The dataset adheres to Schema.org or DCAT metadata standards.; The license and/or any data access restrictions are described in the paper.; The paper includes a convincing justification of the special nature of the dataset that makes it impossible to conform to these suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ICML 2020, lack of adherence to these dataset suggestions is not grounds for rejection and should not affect your score; authors were encouraged to follow these suggestions. Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Comments to Meta-Reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Section for comments that only meta-reviewers ('area chairs') will see; intended for sparing use, particularly for items that may break anonymity of yourself or of the authors (to other reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible only to meta-reviewers. Use sparingly; do not put material here that should be in public review unless it must be confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Paper? (meta-reviewer flag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checkbox to indicate particularly creative papers that study a new problem or involve a very novel idea or insight; checked if reviewer feels the paper is creative enough to be accepted even if there are some weaknesses in execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social/Humanitarian Relevance? (meta-reviewer flag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checkbox to highlight papers that work on problems with strong social or humanitarian relevance; checked if reviewer feels the submission is sufficiently socially relevant to be accepted even if there are weaknesses in execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality agreement (reviewer must agree)
rubrics_metrics.description: I agree to keep the paper and supplementary materials (including code submissions and LaTeX source) confidential, and delete any submitted code at the end of the review cycle to comply with the confidentiality requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required acknowledgment. Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICML code of conduct acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: I acknowledge that my review accords with the ICML code of conduct (see https://icml.cc/public/CodeOfConduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required acknowledgment. Visible to authors during feedback, visible to authors after notification, visible to other reviewers, visible to meta-reviewers.
